correctness.rationale: The squared distance to a fixed vertex along a half-perimeter arc grows strictly on each successive pre-opposite edge and falls on the terminal half of the opposite edge, hence any centered circle intersects each reflected arc at most twice and the total boundary at most four points. For distances between opposite-side midpoint and farthest vertex distances, two crossings on each side arc yield four; original Bárány–Roldán-Pensado lower bound gives H_n(p)>=4 for every boundary p. Sample independent circle-segment enumeration for n=3,5,7,9,15,31 and many radius chambers corroborated; general result uses analytic monotonicity not finite samples.
